title: Roos computation of derived limits of abelian groups
statement: Let $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathbf N)$ be the category of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system] of abelian groups and $\varprojlim:\operatorname{Ab}(\mathbf N)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ the inverse-limit functor. Then $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathbf N)$ is an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives and $\varprojlim$ is left exact additive, so its right derived functors $R^q\varprojlim$ are defined [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For an inverse system $(A_n,f_n:A_{n+1}\to A_n)$ of abelian groups let $1-s:\prod_nA_n\to\prod_nA_n$ be the map $(x_n)_n\mapsto(x_n-f_n(x_{n+1}))_n$. Then, naturally in $(A_n)$, $\varprojlim_nA_n=\ker(1-s)$, $R^1\varprojlim_nA_n\cong\operatorname{coker}(1-s)$, and $R^q\varprojlim_nA_n=0$ for every $q\geq2$.

proof.text: The tower category is abelian by the functor-category instance [lem-pc-tower-abelian] and has enough injectives by [lem-pc-tower-enough-injectives]. Additivity of inverse limit follows directly from the projection equations: after composing with each limit projection, the equation limMap(f+g)=limMap(f)+limMap(g) is the distributivity of composition over addition and the componentwise addition of tower morphisms. Left exactness is supplied by [lem-pc-tower-limit-left-exact]. These properties define the right derived functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. The additive and enough-injectives structural clauses are now proved; the subsequent Roos computation remains to be formalized.

For a tower (A_n,f_n), compatible elements of the product are exactly the tuples satisfying x_n=f_n(x_{n+1}); hence the inverse limit is the kernel of the homomorphism 1-s:(x_n)_n\mapsto(x_n-f_n(x_{n+1}))_n. This identification is natural in morphisms of towers.

Construction (Stacks 07KW, proof). For the tower $(A_n,f_n)_{n\geq1}$ let $B_n=A_n\oplus A_{n-1}\oplus\cdots\oplus A_1$ and $C_n=A_{n-1}\oplus\cdots\oplus A_1$ ($C_1=0$), both with the projections forgetting the first summand as transition maps $B_{n+1}\to B_n$, $C_{n+1}\to C_n$; these transition maps are surjective. Let $A_n\to B_n$ be $a\mapsto(a,f_{n-1}(a),f_{n-2}f_{n-1}(a),\dots,f_1\cdots f_{n-1}(a))$ and $B_n\to C_n$ be $(x_n,\dots,x_1)\mapsto(x_i-f_i(x_{i+1}))_{1\leq i\leq n-1}$; both commute with the transition maps, so they are morphisms of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system]. For each $n$ the sequence $0\to A_n\to B_n\to C_n\to0$ is exact: the first map is injective (first coordinate), the kernel of the second is the set of $(x_i)$ with $x_i=f_i(x_{i+1})$ for $i<n$, which is the image of $A_n$, and the second is surjective (given $(y_i)$ put $x_n=0$ and $x_i=y_i+f_i(x_{i+1})$ downwards). Kernels and cokernels of levelwise homomorphisms in the abelian category of towers [lem-pc-tower-abelian] are the levelwise ones with induced transition maps (these satisfy the universal properties levelwise), so $0\to(A_n)\to(B_n)\to(C_n)\to0$ is a short exact sequence of towers. A compatible family in $\varprojlim B_n$ is $b_n=(x_n,\dots,x_1)$ for a unique $(x_i)\in\prod_iA_i$, so $\varprojlim_nB_n=\prod_nA_n$, likewise $\varprojlim_nC_n=\prod_nA_n$, and under these identifications $\varprojlim(B_n\to C_n)$ is $(x_i)\mapsto(x_i-f_i(x_{i+1}))_i=1-s$, while $\varprojlim(A_n\to B_n)$ is the inclusion $\varprojlim A_n\subseteq\prod_nA_n$ of Step 2. A morphism of towers $(\varphi_n)$ induces $\bigoplus\varphi_i$ on $B_n,C_n$, giving a morphism of these short exact sequences compatible with all identifications.

proof.text: The towers $(B_n)$ and $(C_n)$ of Step 3 have surjective transition maps, so $R^q\varprojlim B_n=R^q\varprojlim C_n=0$ for all $q\geq1$ by [lem-pc-tower-surjective-lim-acyclic]. By Step 1 the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] hold for $v=\varprojlim$ on towers, and with $R^0\varprojlim=\varprojlim$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive] its part (2) gives, for the short exact sequence of Step 3, the exact sequence $0\to\varprojlim A_n\to\varprojlim B_n\to\varprojlim C_n\xrightarrow{\delta}R^1\varprojlim A_n\to R^1\varprojlim B_n=0$ and, for $q\geq2$, $0=R^{q-1}\varprojlim C_n\to R^q\varprojlim A_n\to R^q\varprojlim B_n=0$. With the identifications of Step 3 the first sequence reads $0\to\varprojlim A_n\to\prod_nA_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nA_n\to R^1\varprojlim A_n\to0$, so $\delta$ induces $\operatorname{coker}(1-s)\cong R^1\varprojlim_nA_n$; the second gives $R^q\varprojlim_nA_n=0$ for $q\geq2$. Naturality in $(A_n)$: a morphism of towers gives a morphism of the short exact sequences of Step 3, and the connecting maps are natural by part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor].
